description: Someone listing their own day out loud. Captured from a real device recording, where an over-strict small-talk rule caused every one of these to be dropped.
transcript: So I have one meeting tomorrow at 5. I have one interview at 6 pm. I'll play football at 7.15. And I'll also meet my previous teacher tomorrow. My friend has his birthday the day after tomorrow. Also I have to send a WhatsApp to Priya.

expected_items.quote: So I have one meeting tomorrow at 5.
expected_items.note: A personal appointment is still something to be at. 'I have a meeting' states a fact about the schedule rather than taking work on, so requirement is right. Label corrected: 'I have (to)' names the speaker as owner, so commitment fits the stated rule as well as requirement.

expected_items.quote: I have one interview at 6 pm.
expected_items.note: A time with no day. Must not be guessed into a date. Label corrected: 'I have (to)' names the speaker as owner, so commitment fits the stated rule as well as requirement.

'I'll' is a commitment by the speaker even though it is leisure. '7.15' is not parsed as a time - known gap in core/dates.py, which handles '7.15 pm' but not a bare '7.15'. No deadline is invented, which is the safe failure.

expected_items.quote: I'll also meet my previous teacher tomorrow.
expected_items.note: Personal, but a commitment with a resolvable date.

expected_items.quote: Also I have to send a WhatsApp to Priya.
expected_items.note: 'I have to' is a requirement. No deadline was given, and none should be invented. Label corrected: 'I have (to)' names the speaker as owner, so commitment fits the stated rule as well as requirement.

expected_items.quote: My friend has his birthday the day after tomorrow.
expected_items.note: A date to remember rather than a task. Which act it lands on is not important; capturing the date is.

must_not_extract: nothing at all - the earlier prompt dropped this entire conversation as small talk
